newsitem.title: USA: Hartmarx sees improved Q4, year results.
newsitem.headline: Hartmarx sees improved Q4, year results.

text.p: Hartmarx Corp, which reported higher fiscal 1996 third quarter operating earnings, said Thursday it expects operating results for both the fourth quarter and full year will show improvements over 1995.
Hartmarx reported operating earnings for its fiscal third quarter ended August 31, 1996 rose 46 percent over last year to $5 million.

Net earnings increased to $3.1 million from $2.2 million. Revenues in the third quarter fell slightly to $164.9 million from $166.7 million in the 1995 third quarter, the apparel maker said in a statement.

Hartmarx said fiscal third quarter results benefited from expense and debt reduction. However, revenues were hurt by lower sales to several retail customers currently operating in bankruptcy and the elimination of two small, unprofitable product lines.

Looking ahead, Hartmarx said the suit, sportcoat and dress slack markets appear to be stabilizing with some signs of expanding demand, and the company expects to participate in these improved markets.

"Our retail customers report increasing demand for better tailored clothing products and our re-order sales are robust as a result of strong selling performance at retail," said Elbert Hand, Hartmarx chairman, in a statement.
Hartmarx produces and markets business, casual and golfing apparel.
